requirement:
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.

The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.

Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
rationale:
The implementation and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`.

### Obligations and coverage

- **Wait on transient failure; retry the same completion:** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` invokes `ProviderBackoff::retry`, sleeps, and continues the request loop. `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff]/fn[next_delay]` recognizes HTTP 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504, and each of the four named Bedrock exceptions. Coverage: `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retries_throttling_unavailability_and_timeouts_but_not_permanent_errors]`, `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[transient_bedrock_codes_retry_whatever_their_http_status]`, and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt]`.
- **Abandon an unanswered request after ten minutes:** `src/authoring/mod.rs#const[REQUEST_TIMEOUT]` sets 600 seconds; `converse` wraps each completion in a timeout and treats expiration as transient. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unanswered_requests_are_abandoned_and_retried]` exercises a pending completion followed by successful recovery.
- **Retain prompt; retain history; retain tools; retain pending inputs; do not restart the assessment; do not repeat completed tools:** `converse` retries a clone of the existing request before changing conversation state or dispatching tools. Pending evidence is retained across failures. The unchanged-request assertions in `throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[success_resets_backoff_and_retries_keep_history_without_repeating_tools]` cover the initial request and a request containing completed tool results; the latter also asserts one read-tool invocation and preserved evidence.
- **Keep permanent input/context-length errors as errors; keep authentication failures as errors; keep invalid requests as errors; do not retry merely because a message mentions tokens:** `next_delay` uses structured status/code information, not message matching, and returns no delay for permanent failures. `retries_throttling_unavailability_and_timeouts_but_not_permanent_errors` covers validation, access denial, and token-message rejection. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[permanent_provider_failure_returns_without_waiting_or_retrying]` verifies propagation without delay or a second request.
- **Start the window at one second; double on consecutive transient failures; cap it at sixty seconds; randomly choose each delay between half and all of the window:** `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff/Default]` and `next_delay` implement these properties, using `fastrand` for equal jitter. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[jittered_backoff_grows_to_a_ceiling]` checks the successive bounds through the ceiling.
- **Honor seconds-form Retry-After; honor HTTP-date Retry-After; use it as a minimum even beyond the window:** `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[retry_after]` parses both forms and `next_delay` takes the maximum. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[retry_after_accepts_seconds_and_dates_without_shortening_provider_delay]` checks both formats and a ninety-second minimum. The retry-stop behavior in `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[ProviderBackoff]/fn[retry]` is separately specified by the requirement it marks, `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`, explicitly including Retry-After delays beyond the retry horizon; it is not unspecified behavior here.
- **Reset backoff after success:** `converse` replaces the backoff with its default after a successful response. `success_resets_backoff_and_retries_keep_history_without_repeating_tools` verifies that failures on either side of a successful tool turn both use the initial window.
- **Interruption cancels the wait; interruption cancels further retries:** the awaited sleep and completion remain inside the conversation future, with no detached retry task. `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cancelling_during_backoff_prevents_another_request]` cancels that future during backoff, advances the clock, and verifies no additional request or recorded evidence.
- **Record every attempt under `requirements.authoring.usage_requests`:** `converse` begins and ends a usage request for every iteration and marks retries. `throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt` checks all six attempts, failed/completed outcomes, failure metadata, and unavailable failed-request measurements; `unanswered_requests_are_abandoned_and_retried` covers timeout attempts. This assesses application of the cited usage requirement, not its independent implementation.
- **Disable hidden SDK retries:** `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[bedrock_sdk_config]` reaches `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[bedrock_sdk_loader]`, which explicitly disables AWS retries. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bedrock_sdk_retries_are_disabled]` checks one maximum attempt. The other backend construction uses Rig's direct HTTP transport rather than introducing a harness retry layer.
- **Do not report transient recovery as a finished judgment; do not report it as a terminal assessment error:** the transient branch in `converse` continues before submission processing or error return. The successful multi-failure assessment test verifies eventual completion with one submission; the cancellation test verifies recovery can remain unfinished without another request.
- **Record pending inputs as evidence only after success:** `converse` calls `record_inputs` and clears pending inputs only after obtaining a successful response. The throttled-request test verifies their successful-request index, the tool-turn test verifies retained additional evidence, and the cancellation test verifies no evidence is recorded while recovery has not succeeded.

The retry machinery is reachable through the marked `converse` implementation and the marked Bedrock configuration root. All tests cited above carry the subject's test reference. No acknowledged or unacknowledged gap was found.

:::{req} usage_requests
Usage MUST record each provider request's outcome and available input/output
token counts, including retries, with cached or reasoning-token counts when
provided, and for a failed request the failure under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests.failures`. Missing measurements MUST be recorded as unavailable, not zero.
Run totals MUST include request and tool-call counts by tool, elapsed time, and
available token usage, identifying incomplete totals without double counting
provider counters that overlap.
:::{req} provider
The authoring harness MUST use Rig and support Bedrock, Ollama, and OpenAI. Users MUST be
able to select a backend and model through configuration without changing the
assessment tools, prompt, or evidence format.
:::{req} delivered_inputs
The harness MUST record the sources it supplies to the model, including
mandatory inputs and additional reads, using the evidence input formats
defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs`, and
{cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs`. The harness MUST create these records
itself so ordinary evidence validation can check them later.
:::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
